task-intent.statement: Preserve the native engine worktree guard while restoring crew and MCP workflows broken by the new ambient-cwd comparison.

expected-behavior.statement: A dispatched crew would already run in its assigned worktree and the in-process MCP door would be able to drive a newly opened origin-stamped spine without weakening the guard.

observed-behavior.statement: The frozen ruling's crew-cwd premise was empirically false because run_crew passed no cwd, and the MCP door could not already stand in a worktree that spine_open had only just created; the untouched lifecycle round trip failed.

impact-cost.statement: The implementation reached independent review before the false premise was measured, then the only full-suite failure blocked integration and required a human ruling that expanded the production scope to two cwd owners.

workaround.statement: The run floated the collision with measurements, and the human ruled both repairs; commit 48f07123 now establishes an absolute crew cwd and a narrowly scoped MCP engine cwd.

task-intent.statement: Independently verify that the ruled crew-cwd repair always supplies an absolute assigned worktree to dispatch and resume.

expected-behavior.statement: The focused tests and the crew_cwd docstring's absolute-path contract would cover the real parser defaults as well as absolute temporary roots.

observed-behavior.statement: All original tests supplied an already-absolute temporary root, while the actual default pair root='.' and worktree='.' returned a relative Path; the first fresh reviewer blocked on that exact discrepancy.

impact-cost.statement: One bounded rework and a second independent review were required after an apparently green first repair; without the review probe the production default would have violated the claimed contract.

workaround.statement: The reviewer appended an explicit default-dot criterion; g1c added parser-default dispatch and resume tests, normalized root before joining, and a fresh reviewer approved the repaired boundary.

task-intent.statement: Close the execute integration gate with the same full test suite that passed in the reviewer and a clean shell.

expected-behavior.statement: The engine-owned pytest child would see the normal clean caller environment and reproduce 2981 passing tests.

observed-behavior.statement: The MCP server's SPINE_FILE, SPINE_ENGINE, and SPINE_SESSION bindings were inherited by the pytest child, deterministically failing DC3InheritanceMechanismTests while the same tree passed when those three names were absent.

impact-cost.statement: Two engine advance refusals and one exact reproduction were needed to separate a harness-environment false red from product rework; the frozen gate command could not pass under the selected MCP-first interaction path.

workaround.statement: An Admiral-ratified MCP retext-check changed only g1-integrate.c1 to clear the three door bindings for pytest; the engine then recorded 2981 passed without a waiver.

task-intent.statement: Use the spine MCP server rather than the checklist-engine CLI for every engine interaction in an already-running Codex host.

expected-behavior.statement: The native spine MCP tools or a concise manual-stdio invocation example would be available after the server was added to the harness.

observed-behavior.statement: The host did not hot-load the new MCP tools, and handoffs supplied environment bindings but no initialize, tools/list, or tools/call JSON-RPC envelopes; one guessed tool name also failed before tools/list exposed the actual schema.

impact-cost.statement: Every Commander and replacement-crew engine call required newline-delimited JSON construction and result parsing, and implementers/reviewers independently reconstructed the same protocol.

workaround.statement: The run kept persistent stdio server sessions bound to each exact job file, called tools/list to discover schemas, and used only JSON-RPC MCP calls for engine state changes.

task-intent.statement: Dispatch the required independent reviewer through run_crew after recovery reported no conflicting crew.

expected-behavior.statement: The configured Claude foreground backend would launch and produce the review survey result.

observed-behavior.statement: Claude exited before review work with a weekly-limit message resetting the following day, leaving a recorded attempt that recovery classified as needing explicit abandonment.

impact-cost.statement: The failed attempt had to be recovered and abandoned before another reviewer could be recorded, and the role execution moved to a different backend/model than the initial dispatch.

workaround.statement: The Commander used run_crew's external record-only backend and a Codex reviewer bound to the already-instantiated survey; the durable result was verified through run_crew before integration.

task-intent.statement: Apply bounded TDD and reversible review arms in the assigned sibling worktree using the mandated patch workflow.

expected-behavior.statement: The apply_patch helper would operate in the delegated worktree and temporary directories available to the crew.

observed-behavior.statement: Multiple implementer and reviewer patch-helper attempts failed during bwrap loopback setup for both the sibling worktree and temporary space, before any requested patch content was applied.

impact-cost.statement: At least four failed patch invocations across crews, plus extra byte-hash verification and temporary-copy handling for every deliberate-breakage arm.

workaround.statement: Crews applied bounded reversible git patches and verified pre/post SHA-256 equality; the Commander later used an escalated interactive apply_patch process rooted in the delegated worktree.

task-intent.statement: Drive external implementer and reviewer roles from already-instantiated checklists while preserving role doctrine, generated artifacts, and prior-review criteria.

expected-behavior.statement: The role instructions and handoffs would name the external-launch binding state, manual MCP envelopes, generated-artifact scope, concrete plan imperatives, and prior check meanings.

observed-behavior.statement: External launches carried SPINE_PARENT without a bound role spine, one generic plan imperative remained a placeholder, map regeneration was required but omitted from the allowed-file list, and the re-review cited prior check IDs without restating their imperatives.

impact-cost.statement: Crews had to choose a documented-but-unnamed third binding path, amend the concrete command through MCP, disclose generated map scope, and reconstruct reviewer checks from prior artifacts.

workaround.statement: Each crew recorded its own plan against the supplied checklist, used MCP amendment for the one authorized placeholder command, regenerated and disclosed the map artifact, and appended explicit re-review checks reconstructed from durable results.
